arrive.text: A little town, on a still afternoon. You need to know the time.

notice.text: Market day, Saturday. Choir practice, Thursday. A lost cat. Clock repairs, enquire within.

bench.text: A bench in the sun. The whole town seems to be having a nap.

reads.text: The town clock says two o'clock. It has always kept good time.

asked.text: The postman looks at his watch. It's ticking.

true.text: And the church bell strikes two. It is two o'clock.

stopped.text: The town clock hasn't moved. It stopped at two o'clock yesterday. You happened to look at it in the one minute of the day it was right.

end.text: You believed it. It was true. And you had good reason. So did you know what time it was?

stopped_2.text: The town clock hasn't moved. It stopped yesterday, at two. If you'd looked at that, you'd have believed exactly the same thing.

asked_end.text: But you asked someone whose watch was going. This time, you weren't only right.
